title: Pair Encoding with a Fixed First Component
statement: For every fixed Boolean word $\alpha$, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the pair encoding of $(\alpha,x)$: each bit of $\alpha$ doubled, followed by the separator $01$, followed by $x$.
hypotheses_covered: For every fixed Boolean word alpha
Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the pair encoding of (alpha,x) within c(|x|+1) steps on every input

self-delimiting pair encoding of $(\alpha, x)$ --- each bit of $\alpha$
